properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-14, flipping the proof idea round: "would having both Operation: Modus Ponens and a check in reflow2 checks that Q actually follows from P and P → Q improve any design that reflow2 does?"

WHAT IS ALREADY ON THE RECORD, so part of this is a HOW inside accepted intent:
- req:decomposition-covers-its-parent (accepted). reflow2 already applies ONE inference rule, silently, everywhere: a parent is delivered if and only if EVERY decomposed child is (report.rs, quoted in that requirement). That is an AND that nobody wrote down. Its other half, whether the children cover the parent, is meant to be ASKED of the person, never judged by a model.
- req:assumptions-are-first-class (accepted). "What rests on it is computed." It leaves open "what edge carries 'rests on' (DEPENDS_ON is lateral and already crowded; a dedicated relation may be clearer)". A "follows from" edge is that edge.
- dec:idea-flo2-holds-a-proof-as-a-design-reflow2-records-the-equations-and-a-model-reasons-the-steps, option (h): the same vocabulary addition, raised for proofs.

WHERE IT WOULD IMPROVE AN ORDINARY DESIGN (a sketch):
(a) THE ROLL-UP SAYS ITS RULE. Real designs also need "any one suffices" (redundancy, defence in depth) and "k of n" (voting, quorum), not only AND. Example from flo2 this week: "a published file never runs as a page on flo2.io" holds through EITHER the sandbox CSP OR the file being served as a download of a non-runnable type. Take one away and the claim still holds, with less margin. DEPENDS_ON cannot say which, so a change can't tell BROKEN from WEAKENED.
(b) ASSUMPTIONS FALL PRECISELY. When an assumption fails, the check computes which conclusions lose every path that supported them, and which still stand on another.
(c) THE WARRANT BECOMES A NODE. "P → Q", the reason a premise supports a conclusion, today lives in rationale prose. As a premise of its own, it can be challenged, verified, or go stale.
(d) DECISIONS GO STALE COMPUTABLY. A decision's premises are named, so when one is invalidated, the decision is flagged with WHICH premise.

THE CHECK, in a design (as opposed to a proof): it is PROPOSITIONAL OVER STATUSES. Given each premise's status and the step's rule (AND, OR, k of n, implies), does the conclusion's claimed status follow? That is a truth-table check, mechanical and cheap, and it needs no formal language, because it reads statuses, not prose. It checks the FORM only. Whether each premise is true stays with verification. Whether the children cover the parent stays a question to the person.

PRECEDENT IN ENGINEERING: assurance (safety) cases in Goal Structuring Notation, whose Strategy node is his "Operation" box between a goal and its sub-goals and evidence (used under Def Stan 00-56 and ISO 26262). Fault trees, whose AND/OR gates are the same idea for failure.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(e) A RULE ON THE LINK: an AND / OR / k-of-n value on the support relation, and the roll-up and propagate_change honour it. AND stays the default, so every design reads exactly as today unless someone marks a link otherwise.
(f) AN INFERENCE-STEP NODE as well (rule, premises, conclusion), for warrants that need their own record. That is (c) above, and a proof's modus ponens.
(g) NOTHING NEW: keep writing the rule in prose.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- STRUCTURE IS NOT TRUTH (job 3). A false warrant ("if sandboxed, no script runs", when it doesn't) makes the check pass. The gain is that the warrant is now a node someone can challenge, not that the check makes it true.
- CEREMONY. Most links are fine as AND. If every claim has to name its rule, people stop writing claims. So the default must stay silent, and only an OR or k-of-n is marked.
- VOCABULARY GROWTH against the "fewer things" yardstick. Against that: this serves two accepted requirements already waiting on it, plus proofs, arguments and legal cases. That is the strongest case for new vocabulary on the record.
- THE SURFACE ONLY GROWS. A new value, edge or node is additive, so Alex's MCP keeps working, and the retirement rule is not involved.

SIZE (a finding): (g) nothing. (e) moderate: a property, plus the roll-up and the change walk taught to read it. (f) moderate: a node type and its edges, served to every design.
properties.name: OPEN — would an explicit inference step (an operation with its rule, premises in, conclusion out) and a check that the conclusion follows improve every reflow2 design, not only a proof?
properties.rationale: Asked by Anthony while the proof idea was being recorded, turning it round: whether proof machinery pays for itself in ordinary designs. Recorded with the two accepted requirements it would serve, so it reads as a HOW for existing intent and not as a new direction. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
